corpusSummary: The corpus maps rapid scholarly attention to how generative AI and large language models intersect with decision-making, work, education, health, and public discourse. It highlights trust, embodiment, and social dynamics of AI adoption; methodological use of LLMs as research tools with governance considerations; education and AI literacy in pedagogy and assessment; and safety, bias, and misinformation challenges across domains, alongside evaluation and governance frameworks for responsible deployment.

themes.name: Socio-technical AI adoption and interaction
themes.description: Papers explore AI-in-use, embodiment, trust formation, and social influence shaping adoption in work, health, parenting, travel, and everyday decision-making.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and governance
themes.description: A growing strand proposes LLM-based workflows, data pipelines, fairness checks, and governance frameworks to validate, document, and ethically oversee AI-enabled research.

themes.name: AI in education and AI literacy
themes.description: Studies examine AI’s impact on STEM learning, pedagogy, assessment practices, and AI literacy for diverse learners, including older adults and rural educators.

themes.name: Safety, bias, and misinformation in AI outputs
themes.description: Research interrogates the quality, safety, and bias of AI-generated content across health, media, and public discourse, including misinformation and deepfake warnings.

emergingKeywords: Education-tech and assessment in AI era
